svg.text: N.E.D.S — Smart Lathi: complete system schematic (rev C)
Team Venjex · SIH 2026 · PS 26026 — eight 16-bit gas channels on two ADS1115 converters, environmental compensation, thermal-desorption heater, pump, GPS, battery monitoring & protected power chain.
Filled dot = junction. Plain crossing = not connected. Every 5 V sensor output passes its own 10k/10k divider before it reaches a 3.3 V input.
Every 5 V sensor output passes a 10k/10k divider before reaching a 16-bit ADS1115 ADC.
GPIO34, GPIO36 and GPIO39 are now free spare analog inputs
8.4 V max → 1.95 V to ESP32 ADC
Supplies eight 16-bit gas channels plus temperature and humidity
figures that correct every MQ reading for drift.
R19 holds the P-MOSFET OFF until Q4 pulls its gate down,
so the sensor rail is dead while the ESP32 boots.
D1 shorts the collapsing-field spike the moment the pump switches off.
Leave it out and that spike resets or destroys the ESP32.
Proves the mesh really reaches 180 °C. Without it
the duty-cycle figure in the deck is just an assertion.
Stamps every alert with position and UTC time — the
traceable evidence trail an NDPS case needs.
A Pi 4 draws 1.2–2.0 A by itself. Share the LM2596 with it and it
browns out mid-scan, which shows up as a corrupted SD card.
RF / SVM inference · Flask dashboard · SQLite evidence log
WIRED UART FALLBACK — GPIO33/32 active when Wi-Fi signal is lost. Cross pair: ESP32 TX -> Pi RX, ESP32 RX <- Pi TX. Both see 3.3 V logic levels.
Wi-Fi · MQTT to neds/neds-01/sensors, one reading per second — the primary link
Wi-Fi is the primary link. If signal drops, GPIO33/32 picks up via wired UART.
C2 sits beside the heater and absorbs the 180 °C burst current.
C3–C5: 100 nF decoupling — one at each ADS1115, BME688 and the MAX6675.
What changed in rev C, and why nothing burns
Two ADS1115 converters replace the ESP32's own ADC: eight 16-bit channels instead of six 12-bit ones, so the MiCS-6814's CO and NH₃ elements are finally read.
GPIO35 measures Vbat (33k/10k). Wired UART fallback to Pi (pin 8/10); GPIO33/32 picks up if Wi-Fi drops. GPIO34, 36 and 39 stay spare.
Discharge protection: R1–R24 halve every sensor output. R13–R15 limit gate current. R16–R19 hold all three MOSFETs OFF at boot. D1 flyback. D2 reverse-polarity. D3 TVS. F1 fuse. SW1 master cut-off.
